title: Share Trading Policy
date_approved: Authorised for release by the Board; the policy may be amended by resolution of the Board, and the Company Secretary is authorised to make administrative or consequential amendments of no material significance
date_next_review: The Board will review this policy from time to time; no date stated

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors, officers, other Key Management Personnel, employees and contractors of Medibank, and any other person designated by the Company Secretary. Only section 3 (insider trading) and section 10 (confidential information) apply to this tier generally, together with the hortatory statement in 6.2(a) that Employees should not engage in short term or speculative trading. No blackout, notification, hedging or financing restriction applies to an Employee who is not a Restricted Employee.

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Employees likely to come in contact with key financial, operational and strategic information about Medibank. Automatically includes Directors; the Company Secretary; members of the Group Squad and all other direct reports to the CEO; direct reports to the Group Squad; direct reports to the Hub Lead - Financial Control and to the Head of Financial Accounting; direct reports to the Hub Lead - Actuarial Services & Chief Actuary; direct reports to the Hub Lead - Group Strategy & Chief Strategy Officer; members of the Trust, Legal and Compliance, Commercial Finance, Treasury, Investor Relations and External Affairs teams; and any other Key Management Personnel. The Company Secretary may nominate additional individuals and maintains a continuously updated register. Sections 3 to 9 apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; a Restricted Employee distinguished only by the notification officer (Chair of the Audit Committee, copied to the Company Secretary) and, as a non-executive director, by exemption from the Request to Deal form.

tiers.name: Other directors (including CEO)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, including the CEO; notify the Chair of the Board, copied to the Company Secretary. Non-executive directors in this group are exempt from the Request to Deal form.

tiers.name: Members of Group Squad
tiers.description: Members of the Group Squad led by the CEO; notify the CEO or Company Secretary and must complete the Request to Deal form.

tiers.name: Other Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Restricted Employees other than directors, the CEO and Group Squad members; notify the Company Secretary or his or her delegate and must complete the Request to Deal form.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner; child or step-child under 18; a relative sharing the same household for at least 12 months at the date of the transaction; any other entity of which the Restricted Employee is a director, secretary or executive officer (unless insulated by appropriate arrangements); companies in which the Restricted Employee holds at least 20% of share capital or controls at least 20% of voting power; a trustee where the beneficiaries include the Restricted Employee, spouse, partner or minor child; and any other persons over whom the Restricted Employee has or may be expected to have investment control or influence. Section 8 applies only where the Restricted Employee has investment control over the Associate's dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested; or (ii) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: close of trading on the business day after Medibank's half yearly results are announced to ASX
close of trading on the business day after Medibank's annual results are announced to ASX

windows.start_anchor: any extension to a closed period, and any additional period, as specified by the Board

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any extension to a closed period and any additional period, which then form part of the defined Blackout Periods. The policy does not say whether such an extension or additional period is announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Section 6.3(b) is a standing ban on dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and section 6.4 defines those to include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties. There is no venue limit, so a bank-written OTC put and call are squarely caught, and the ban is not conditioned on the vesting state of any underlying shares. The only escape is 'the type of dealing permitted under this policy', which means the section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Employee must not: ... deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Medibank shares are equally caught by 6.3(b), and are independently Medibank Securities because their value is materially determined by reference to Medibank.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this section, financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: The scope clause confines sections 4 to 9, including the section 6 further restrictions, to Restricted Employees. An Employee outside the register is bound only by the insider trading prohibition and the confidentiality obligation, plus the hortatory 6.2(a) statement about short term and speculative trading.
rules.evidence: section 3 (insider trading) and section 10 (confidential information) apply to everyone (including all Employees, contractors and agents of Medibank); sections 3 to 7 (share trading policy), section 8 (process for trading) and section 9 (associates) apply to all Restricted Employees

rules.detail: Remuneration-based hedging ban expressed at the widest level: any transaction or arrangement with anyone which could have the effect of limiting risk exposure to unvested remuneration. No consent route and, because section 7.1(b) relief is limited to disposals, no exceptional-circumstances route either.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Employee must not: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested

rules.detail: Vested remuneration that remains subject to a holding lock is treated identically to unvested remuneration for hedging purposes.
rules.evidence: has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The remuneration limb in 6.3(a) stops at holding-locked shares, but 6.3(b) independently bans dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and any hedge of vested unrestricted shares must be executed through such a product. Shares bought on market are therefore no more hedgeable than plan shares.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly in the 6.4 list of financial products, so a prepaid forward, forward sale or share swap over Medibank shares is prohibited. A monetisation structured purely as a secured loan without a derivative is instead permitted with Company Secretary consent under 6.1(b).
rules.evidence: financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Flat ban with no approval route, footnoted by reference to ASIC Regulatory Guide 196 and defined as selling financial products you do not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees are not permitted to engage in short selling of Medibank Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned. It is not a financial product under 6.4, not a funding arrangement with Medibank Securities as security under 6.1(b), and not within the description of dealing.

Contracts for difference are named in the 6.4 definition of financial products, so they fall within the standing 6.3(b) prohibition; a short CFD would also breach the short selling ban and, if closed within 90 days, the minimum holding period.
rules.evidence: derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties

rules.detail: Absolute ban with no consent route, expressly justified by the risk that the facility terms may force a sale during a Blackout Period or while the holder has Inside Information. The Relevant Notification Officer is the arbiter of whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement, which matters because the borderline with a 6.1(b) consented facility is where a collar loan sits.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Medibank Securities as the terms may require Medibank Securities to be sold during a Blackout Period or when the Restricted Employee possesses Inside Information.

rules.detail: Granting security over Medibank Securities is permitted with the consent of the Company Secretary. The clause is drafted so broadly that even an incidental 'all assets' security interest that happens to catch Medibank shares requires consent. No form, deadline, validity period or criteria for consent are specified.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must not, without the consent of the Company Secretary, enter into any other funding arrangements where Medibank Securities may be included as security (for example any lending arrangement that involves the Restricted Employee granting an 'all assets' security interest to secure the repayment of a loan).

rules.detail: Secured financing other than margin lending is available with Company Secretary consent, and a lender's enforcement sale under a consented facility is a Permitted Dealing excluded from the Blackout Periods and the notification process. The carve-out is expressly withheld for margin lending agreements and other funding arrangements prohibited by the policy, so the consent is what makes lender enforcement safe.
rules.evidence: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy

rules.detail: Hard 90 day minimum holding period applying to Medibank Securities and, notably, to financial products associated with Medibank Securities, so any derivative position would itself have to be held for at least 90 days. Securities granted under an employee incentive scheme are deemed held from the date of grant, which shortens the wait after vesting.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees must hold any Medibank Securities or financial products associated with Medibank Securities for at least 90 days.

clearance.evidence: In addition, all Restricted Employees, other than non-executive directors, must provide the Relevant Notification Officer with a completed “Request to Deal in Medibank Securities” form, which can be found on the Medibank Intranet Corporate Governance page.

clearance.evidence: Where a Restricted Employee proposes to deal in Medibank Securities in accordance with this policy (including entering into an agreement to deal), they must first provide: written notice of their intention to deal, to the Relevant Notification Officer listed below

clearance.approver: Company Secretary and his or her delegate
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three (3) business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: confirmation that they are not in possession of Inside Information.

clearance.approver: The applicable Relevant Notification Officer for the Restricted Employee who has investment control over the Associate's dealings in Medibank Securities
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three (3) business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: This section 8, including the requirement to provide the Relevant Notification Officer with a completed “Request to Deal in Medibank Securities” form, applies to an Associate in circumstances where a Restricted Employee has investment control over the Associate's dealings in Medibank Securities.
section 8 (process for trading) and section 9 (associates) apply to all Restricted Employees

short_term.basis: at least 90 days, applying to Medibank Securities and to financial products associated with Medibank Securities; securities granted under an employee incentive scheme are deemed to have been held from the date of grant
carve_outs: Medibank Securities granted under an employee incentive scheme are deemed to have been held from the date of grant
the section 5 Permitted Dealings, which are excluded from the operation of section 4

exceptions.evidence: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy

exceptions.approver: Relevant Notification Officer, with 'other exceptional circumstances' determined by the Chair of the Board (or Chair of the Audit Committee where the Chair of the Board is involved)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, for example, a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Medibank Securities
requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements

(beneficial holdings) dealings which do not result in a change in beneficial control of Medibank Securities (for example, transferring a personal holding of Medibank Securities to a personal superannuation fund)

(third parties) an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Medibank Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
(takeover) a disposal of Medibank Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement or acceptance of a takeover offer

exceptions.approver: Board (approval of the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: (security purchase plans and dividend reinvestment plans) trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board

(incentive scheme) the exercise (but not the sale of Medibank Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Blackout Period and the Restricted Employee could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time outside of a Blackout Period.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance, but the stated rationale for the margin lending ban is that 'the terms may require Medibank Securities to be sold during a Blackout Period or when the Restricted Employee possesses Inside Information'. A facility whose terms cannot force a sale on a price trigger is therefore materially easier to characterise as a consentable 6.1(b) funding arrangement rather than a prohibited margin lending arrangement, and the Relevant Notification Officer is expressly the arbiter of that classification.
financing_disclosure: Restricted Employees; inception (before entering into any funding arrangement where Medibank Securities may be included as security, including an 'all assets' security interest); to the Company Secretary; prior consent required, no deadline or form specified (section 6.1(b))
Restricted Employees; classification query (uncertainty whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement); to the Relevant Notification Officer; no deadline specified (section 6.1(a))

exemption_authority: The Relevant Notification Officer may give prior confirmation, in exceptional circumstances, for a Restricted Employee to deal during a Blackout Period, or to dispose of Medibank Securities even if otherwise prohibited under section 6. Exceptional circumstances may include severe financial hardship, court orders or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements, or other circumstances determined by the Chair of the Board (or Chair of the Audit Committee where the Chair of the Board is involved); the discretion must be exercised with caution where there is doubt, and the dealing must be confirmed in writing within three business days. Crucially the section 7.1(b) relief is limited to disposals, so it cannot authorise entry into a hedge, derivative or financing that section 6 prohibits. Separately, the Company Secretary may consent under 6.1(b) to a funding arrangement secured on Medibank Securities.

bespoke_clauses.topic: standing ban on all associated financial products
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Employee must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: it is unqualified as to vesting state and venue, and the only carve-out is the closed list of section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purposes of this section, financial products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Third-party created OTC instruments are expressly within scope, so a bank-written put and call over Medibank shares cannot be argued outside the prohibition on the basis that they are not exchange traded.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition, Restricted Employees must not, without the consent of the Company Secretary, enter into any other funding arrangements where Medibank Securities may be included as security (for example any lending arrangement that involves the Restricted Employee granting an 'all assets' security interest to secure the repayment of a loan).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The funding leg of a collar is available with Company Secretary consent, so a plain loan secured on Medibank shares is possible even though the hedge is not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: consented lender enforcement is a permitted dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Medibank Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement or other funding arrangements, where such arrangements are prohibited by this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by a bank under a facility consented to under 6.1(b) is excluded from the Blackout Periods and the notification process, but enforcement under any facility the policy prohibits is not protected, which makes obtaining the Company Secretary's consent the single most important condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees should consult the Relevant Notification Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Whether a collar loan is a prohibited margin lending arrangement or a consentable 6.1(b) funding arrangement is decided by the company, not the bank, so the classification should be confirmed in writing before the facility is documented.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Employee may request, and the Relevant Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Restricted Employee to: (a) deal in Medibank Securities during a Blackout Period; or (b) dispose of Medibank Securities even if otherwise prohibited under section 6
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only relief from section 6 is a disposal, so no exceptional circumstance, however severe, can authorise entering a hedge, derivative or prohibited financing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ninety day hold applies to the derivative itself
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees must hold any Medibank Securities or financial products associated with Medibank Securities for at least 90 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the derivative ban were relaxed, the collar position itself would have to be held for at least 90 days, ruling out short-dated or early-terminable structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Medibank Securities" means Securities of, or whose value is materially determined by reference to, Medibank.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Instruments whose value tracks the Medibank share price are Medibank Securities in their own right, so the clearance, blackout and 90 day holding rules attach to them directly and not only through the section 6 prohibition; note the general Securities definition is limited to products 'able to be traded on a financial market', a tension the section 6.4 definition overrides for section 6 purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: companies with which the Restricted Employee is connected by directly or indirectly: (i) holding at least 20% of the share capital; or (ii) controlling the exercise of at least 20% of the voting power ... a trustee where the beneficiaries of the trust include the Restricted Employee or his or her spouse, partner or child or step-child under the age of 18
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A 20% shareholding threshold and any family trust are enough to make a counterparty entity an Associate, so booking the collar or the loan away from the individual does not avoid the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance expires five (5) business days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date. ... Restricted Employees must confirm in writing to the Relevant Notification Officer, within three (3) business days of the dealing in Medibank Securities, the number of Medibank Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any permitted leg must be executed within 5 business days of clearance and the bank's identity as counterparty must be disclosed to the company within 3 business days, since 'the relevant parties to the dealing' must be reported.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a Medibank director or executive, because the hedge is prohibited even though the loan is not. Section 6.3(b) bans a Restricted Employee from dealing at any time in financial products associated with Medibank Securities, and section 6.4 defines those to include derivatives, options, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference created over or associated with Medibank Securities by third parties, with no venue limit and no vesting qualification; the only carve-out is the closed list of section 5 Permitted Dealings, none of which is a derivative, and the section 7 exceptional-circumstances relief from section 6 extends only to disposals, so no hardship application can authorise entry into a collar. The funding leg by contrast is workable: margin lending is banned outright, but section 6.1(b) permits any other funding arrangement in which Medibank Securities may be included as security with the consent of the Company Secretary, and section 5(e) then treats a disposal resulting from that lender exercising its rights as a Permitted Dealing outside the Blackout Periods, provided the facility is a consented one rather than a prohibited margin lending arrangement. A bank should therefore expect to be able to offer a secured loan against vested Medibank shares, subject to written Company Secretary consent and to confirming with the Relevant Notification Officer that the facility is not classified as margin lending, but not the put and call legs. Any permitted dealing must also fall outside the 1 January and 1 July Blackout Periods and any Board-specified extension, be cleared in advance by the applicable Relevant Notification Officer within a 5 business day clearance window, be confirmed in writing within 3 business days identifying the counterparty, and respect the 90 day minimum holding period, which applies to associated financial products as well as to shares.
